correctness.rationale: For the exact PGF from the published BPL model, the derived logarithmic coefficients are \(\nu_k=(2q^k-r^k+(-1)^{k+1}b^k)/k\). Negative even coefficients when \(b>q\) rule out additive infinite divisibility. In the \(b\le q\) domain all coefficients are strictly positive and summable; Steutel–van Harn (1979) implies thinning self-decomposability exactly when \(v_k=k\nu_k\) decreases. For even \(k\ge2\) the normalized difference \(A-U(r/q)^k-V(b/q)^k\) is smallest at \(k=2\). The inequality there also forces strictly positive normalized odd differences for every odd \(k\ge3\); \(k=1\) is the other test. Boundary non-strict inequalities, normalization, and the explicit batch PGF were checked algebraically. An independent exact rational script checks 648 parameter combinations and the witness but is not the all-index proof.

originality.rationale: The proposed statement is the exact three-inequality equivalence for thinning self-decomposability, not a claim to the source model, its PGF, additive infinite divisibility, or the general canonical-sequence criterion. Full accessible primary BPL sections contain PGF and statistical properties but not this finite reduction. The separate 1979 characterization requires infinitely many canonical comparisons, and the exact two-index sufficiency here is demonstrated by a parameter-specific exponential monotonicity argument. The weaker additive infinite-divisibility condition obtained directly from the same PGF \(b\le q\) is strictly weaker: at \(\theta=1/10\), \(b=0,1/10,1/3\) all satisfy it but only \(b=1/10\) passes the two further inequalities.

value.rationale: A complete two-parameter, infinitely indexed thinning-admissibility problem for an established count model reduces to three elementary inequalities; this is a natural exact classification, not an arbitrary parameter slice. At \(\theta=1/10\), three exact additive-infinitely-divisible examples show that adding a Bernoulli event first creates and then destroys thinning self-decomposability. This distinguishes a stronger stationarity-building property from ordinary infinite divisibility; the derived batch-size PGF supplies an actual continuous-time immigration/death representation. The same finite tests apply without numerical scanning even on boundary parameters.
